[A815]

## Contents

- **[Status](#status)** — Green/WIP/blocked, test tally, and `branch` -> `dev-soft-core`.
- **[Linked Issue / roles](#linked-issue--roles)** — Public task, executor, and independent reviewers.
- **[Description](#description)** — What changed and why.
- **[Authoritative references](#authoritative-references)** — Requirements/specification clauses and docs.
- **[How to get into the same state](#how-to-get-into-the-same-state)** — Copy-pasteable checkout/dependency/environment commands.
- **[How to validate](#how-to-validate)** — Exact reviewer commands and expected result.
- **[Known limitations / out of scope](#known-limitations--out-of-scope)** — What this deliberately does not do, and why.
- **[Definition of Done](#definition-of-done)** — The merge bar from [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Status

GREEN for review (round 3) — 27 commits, head `dd163e41`; R880-2's and R879-2's findings answered: the identity packet re-published whole (five operands re-encoded so the archive keeps them) and replayable from its published form, the resource sweep's self-test covering its prepare/export wiring, the remaining shipping labels retired; the image identity, the flip check, the timing floor (best of three directives) and every local gate pass, apart from the recorded CI-environment rows — `665-s13-flip-default` -> `dev-soft-core`

## Linked Issue / roles

Relates to #665

Executor: `[A815]`
Internal cleared-context reviewer: `[R<n>]` (assigned by the manager)
External reviewer: `[R<n>]` (assigned by the manager)

## Description

The Mark II split flip (#665 S13). The split placement becomes the shipping default for the two AX7101 shapes the
bench gate qualified (1x1/1if and 8x8/1if), and a split image reads VERSION major 3. The all-fabric placement stays
built and gated behind its switch, so the flip reverts in one commit. The processor is deleted only after the full
qualification (NFR-SCOUT-02), not here.

| Piece | Change |
|---|---|
| Version chain | `milan_csr.sv` states `VERSION_SPLIT_MAJOR = 16'h0003` beside `VERSION`; the datapath's `CTRL_SPLIT_P` selects it, so a split image reads `0x0003_0060` and an all-fabric one `0x0002_0060` (one minor, stated once). VERSION reaches the fabric only as the CSR defaults ROM's word for `0x004`. The ENTITY `firmware_version` is derived at the config's placement: 3.96.0 split, 2.96.0 all-fabric |
| Defaults | `configs/endstation_ax7101_1x1_tdm8.yaml` and `_8x8.yaml` state `control: {placement: split}`; the Arty configs stay all-fabric. The tracked AX7101 sweep fragment is regenerated from the 1x1 config, and `sweep.sh`'s AX7101 row carries the split |
| The switch | `endstation_builder.py <config> --placement all-fabric`, and `BUILD_PLACEMENT=all-fabric ./build.sh ax7101` for the release image. Any `--placement` recipe refuses `--write-rtl` and `--write-fragment`, so tracked files follow the config's own placement |
| Identity | The split manifest records the split VERSION; the identity gate reads a manifest's VERSION at the placement it claims, the placement rule holding the datapath to it |
| Simulations | `sim_split.cpp` pins the split datapath's VERSION `0x0003_0060` and major 3, with a planted defect in `split_mutants.py`; `milan_dp/sim_main.cpp` adds the all-fabric major 2 beside its full word; the split stand-ins (split boot, reboot, service hooks, platform unit bus) answer `0x0003_0060`; the UART grader accepts major 2 or 3 at minor ≥ `0x0056` |
| Gates | Builder gates 23n and 23o hold the AX7101 configs at the split and the rest all-fabric, both recipes and the firmware-string difference; 23m, 1e and 23g elaborate the split recipes with a synthetic platform image and keep the all-fabric builds; 24 and 25c read the string per placement; the entity-shape gate checks it per placement; the feature ledger's current version is the shipping split image's; the clock-constraint probe elaborates the split at both shapes and the all-fabric release; the publication census reads each config's all-fabric build; the control-memory test starts from the all-fabric argv. Each new rule carries a planted defect |
| Tools the flip moved | The #649 resource sweep prices the placement its plan names (all-fabric, the recorded figures' placement) and refuses, before any export, an argv naming a platform image the tree does not hold; the CPU-budget harness replaces the split config's image pair with its own instead of appending a second, so its export argv is the measured run's again |
| Docs | Every "which placement ships" statement, the split contract's section 7, the feature ledger rows, the generated register map (its memory map and build parameters labelled as the recorded all-fabric build's, the split's map pointed at), the README's pipeline picture (labelled the all-fabric release flow, the split build stated beside it), the changelog, `BUILDING.md`, the builder key table, and the documentation inventory (D0-001, D0-033 and D0-056 retired: the default they contradicted is now the split) |

## Authoritative references

- NFR-SCOUT-02 ([FR_NFR.md 3.4](docs/reference/FR_NFR.md)).
- [ARCHITECTURE_HW_SW_SPLIT.md section 7](docs/ARCHITECTURE_HW_SW_SPLIT.md#7-version-and-default-flip): major
  `0x0003` only for split images, all-fabric keeps its identity, MINOR flat, the version chain and its simulations.
- #665: the flip plan's item 6 (issuecomment-6799253003); owner decisions issuecomment-6410301079 (the flip changes
  the default and sets VERSION major 3; all-fabric stays built and gated), -6845315282 (8x8/1if a must, 2if
  optional), -6930885185 (#818's floor), -7044585511 (the 1x1/1if rows); the bench re-check issuecomment-7063917242.

## How to get into the same state

```sh
git fetch origin dd163e41438acb86e0c4d4e76df90f3f91ace1c0 && git checkout --detach FETCH_HEAD   # the reviewed head (branch 665-s13-flip-default)
test "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" = dd163e41438acb86e0c4d4e76df90f3f91ace1c0
git submodule update --init protocol-processor gptp-processor third_party/verilog-axis third_party/tsn-c-stack
python3 sw/builder/endstation_builder.py configs/endstation_ax7101_1x1_tdm8.yaml                        # split
python3 sw/builder/endstation_builder.py configs/endstation_ax7101_1x1_tdm8.yaml --placement all-fabric # release
```

## How to validate

```sh
python3 sw/builder/test_builder.py --require-rv32 --require-elaboration   # gates 23m-23p among them
python3 scripts/check_entity_shape.py --self-test
python3 scripts/check_feature_status.py --self-test
python3 scripts/check_sweep_shape.py --self-test
python3 scripts/baremetal_uart_smoke.py --self-test
python3 syn/resmap/soc_sweep.py --selftest
python3 tb/verilator/ctrl_service_budget/run.py --self-test
(cd tb/verilator/milan_dp && make split && python3 split_mutants.py)
python3 -B tb/verilator/ctrl_service_budget/flip_grade.py --check --point 1x1/1if
python3 -B tb/verilator/ctrl_service_budget/flip_grade.py --check --point 8x8/1if
python3 -B tb/verilator/ctrl_service_budget/load_grade.py --check
bash scripts/run_all_suites.sh <logs> --wait
```

Expected result / pass criteria:

- The builder suite prints `ALL GATES PASS EXCEPT 2 NOT RUN` (a make that does not re-read MAKEFLAGS; gate 11's
  calibration report, which is bench-local); the four self-tests and the split leg pass, and `split_mutants.py`
  catches 32 of 32.
- `flip_grade.py --check --point 1x1/1if` and `--point 8x8/1if` print `RESULT: PASS`: 1x1/1if load 0.511 (0.70),
  last queued notice 127.31 ms (tree 130, owner 140), ACMP 29.06 ms (30), txL 47.88 ms (49); 8x8/1if load 0.744
  (0.75). `--check` alone reports 8x8/2if (reported, not held), byte-identical to dev-soft-core's.
- The sweep: every suite PASS (65; at this head's evidence 51 in the sharded sweep and 14 rerun alone after the wall
  clock killed them under host load).

The evidence, with each command, head and receipt, is posted with the review-ready comment on #665: the image
identity of both bench-gated images (only the VERSION word, the firmware string and the integrity words computed
over them change; netlist, placement and routing are the bench images'), the timing floor at every corner, the
release (all-fabric) export, the CPU-budget harness images and the re-measured descriptor groups.

## Known limitations / out of scope

- The processor is not deleted (NFR-SCOUT-02: after the full qualification). NFR-SCOUT-02 and REQUIREMENTS section 1
  tie deletion to "the switch-over"; this PR follows #665 issuecomment-6410301079 (the flip changes the default)
  and restates REQUIREMENTS section 1 to that order. The normative NFR-SCOUT-02 row is not edited: for the owner.
- The Arty configs stay all-fabric: the bench gate covered only the two AX7101 shapes.
- The full CPU-budget harness re-measure (64 parts a point) is not run: the identity packet published with round
  3's review-ready comment holds the 16 image pairs, the 13 re-measured groups' operands and a replay showing they
  differ only in the firmware string and its CRC (`python3 -I tools/replay.py .` inside the packet).
- The register map keeps its recorded all-fabric SoC export; its memory map and build parameters are labelled as
  that build's and point at the split's map. Re-recording it from a split export restates the memory map and the
  0x920 window: a follow-up Issue, to be opened by the manager.
- The resource map (#649) still prices the all-fabric SoC, the placement its figures were recorded at; pricing the
  split SoC is new measurement work, not this PR's.
- #954 (GET_TX_STATE REGISTERING_FAILED at 1x1/1if) is the first PR after this one, as decided.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Linked Issue acceptance criteria are satisfied
- [ ] New or changed behavior has self-checking tests
- [ ] Required local verification bar passes
- [ ] Self-test evidence is posted in a PR comment
- [ ] No undocumented requirement or interface change remains
- [ ] Internal cleared-context review is positive
- [ ] External review is positive
- [ ] Blocking and major findings are fixed and re-reviewed
- [ ] No review round remains in flight
- [ ] Candidate merge result is validated per [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [ ] Documentation is updated where needed
- [ ] Post-merge containment will be checked before the Issue moves to Done

## Updated 2026-10-31: owner decisions

- **The protocol processor is removed** (16:33). This firmware becomes the only implementation of ADP, ACMP, MAAP, SRP, AECP and saved-state handling. No retained-fabric option stays in the end state. The all-fabric default stays only until this firmware passes the bench qualification; at the switch-over `KL_pp_shadow` is deleted.
- **gPTP moves to firmware** (16:51, 17:04), using `flexptpd`, the implementation the test machine runs. Its source and licence get confirmed before adoption: it is not in the public tsn-c-stack repository. The fabric keeps hardware timestamping on both ports. New lane **F6, gPTP**, below.
- **The fabric keeps:** framing and timestamps on both ports, the time-multiplexed stream engines (crossbar, AVTP/AAF endpoints), the media clock, the frame filtering (TCAM and the mailbox ingress filter), the hard-deadline timers, and `milan_csr` for information and diagnostics.
- **Shape: 32x32 streams** (16x16 logical, each redundant on both networks). Every protocol's service-latency bound is stated and tested at this load: four times the 8x8 load, with 64 streams.
- **Area target:** below 20,000 LUTs for the whole image, recorded on #640.
- **Start:** right after the current release tasks (the merge train and the qualification pre-run).

### Lane added

- **F6, gPTP** (IEEE 802.1AS-2011 with Cor1 and Cor2, as profiled by Milan v1.2):
  - `flexptpd` ported to the core behind the HAL, on the fabric's hardware timestamps for both ports;
  - the gPTP qualification and the #117 bench boxes re-run on it;
  - the fast-reaction and GM-recovery directives apply.

### Superseded below

- "The fabric keeps the gPTP plane": the timestamps stay, the protocol moves (F6).
- "Everything lands behind a build switch whose default is the current all-fabric placement": that holds only until the bench qualification of the firmware.

---

## Original text (2026-10-05)

**Owner direction, 2026-10-05:** write the software side of the Mark II split now, in parallel with the protocol-processor program. The requirement change (#664) still waits for the PP program to finish.

## Scope

Bare-metal firmware on the on-chip RISC-V for:
- **ADP**;
- **ACMP** (decided earlier the same day);
- **MAAP**;
- **SRP** (MRP, with MSRP and MVRP);
- **AECP**: descriptor serving, commands, and the unsolicited notifications. The owner added AECP the same day;
- **the NV memory handling**: read the saved entity state from the flash at boot, apply it, and write it back on change (the #70 saved-state design).

It sits behind the packet-mailbox and ingress-filter contract recorded on #640: block RAM rings, doorbell and interrupt, 32-bit accesses, no DMA, a bus adapter per host, portable C behind a small HAL, one YAML contract. It must port to a hard core.

The fabric keeps:
- framing and timestamps;
- the gPTP plane;
- the timers that carry hard deadlines, posted to the core as events;
- the ingress filter.

## Rules while #664 is open

- Everything lands behind a build switch whose default is the current all-fabric placement. No shipping-image change.
- The firmware builds and is tested on the host against a mailbox model. The existing processor suites' stimulus is reused through that model wherever possible, so each protocol's checks carry over.
- Each protocol states its firmware service-latency bound per response path and tests it, as NFR-SCOUT-03 will require after #664.
- Portable C (C11), no compiler intrinsics in protocol code, and a fixed-width, byte-order-explicit wire layer.

## Lanes (in order)

- **F0, the contract and harness (first).** The mailbox and ingress-filter YAML contract and its generator (fabric module skeleton, C header, docs), the HAL, the host mailbox model and test harness. The ADP firmware is the first vertical slice through it.
- **F1, NV memory handling.** Flash read at boot, validation per the #70 saved-state format (KLJ2), apply, and the write and commit path, ported from `sw/firmware/milan_baremetal` and the processor writer's rules. It can start alongside F0 against the HAL draft.
- **F2, MAAP.**
- **F3, ACMP.**
- **F4, SRP (MRP, MSRP, MVRP).**
- **F5, AECP** (descriptor serving, commands, notifications).

F2 to F5 start once F0's contract merges, so the protocols share one interface.

Relates to #640, #664, #70, and milestone 13.

[A10] **Owner clarification, 2026-10-26: the all-fabric placement stays a permanent, supported build choice.**

- **Class G** in the S1 census means "unused in the split build", not deleted: a generate branch with tie-offs. The all-fabric build instantiates `KL_pp_shadow`, the #637 map writer and restore (`amr_fsm`) and every face as today.
- **S6** omits those modules from the split build only. In the all-fabric build they stay, because there the fabric processor performs the #637 restore. S6's acceptance: both placements build from one tree and one key, and both pass their gates.
- **Every split-lane PR** keeps the all-fabric export byte-identical for every shipped config, as S1 item 5 says.
- **The flip (S13)** changes only the default and sets VERSION major 3. All-fabric remains buildable, and both placements keep their gates after the flip.

[A10] Owner decision, 2026-10-31 16:33, on the module boundaries for the split:

- **The protocol processor is removed.** ADP, ACMP, MAAP, SRP, AECP and NVM serialisation (`KL_pp_shadow` plus MAAP, 24,835 LUTs on the current 1x1 image) become CPU software only. No retained-fabric processor in the end state.
- **The gPTP engine stays in fabric** for now (`KL_gptp_shadow`, 5,194 LUTs).
- **The CSR file is kept for information and diagnostics.** It shrinks as the protocol tables leave. The diagnostics stay in fabric and are read through it.
- **milan_dp's target content:** the crossbar (channel maps, TDM capture and render, render queue) and the AVTP/AAF stream endpoints, about 3.3k LUTs today. The media clock and the time/MAC plane stay in fabric as sibling blocks.

Manager default, unless the owner says otherwise: the fabric processor stays in the default image only until the software passes the bench qualification, then it is deleted at the flip. The split contract (`docs/ARCHITECTURE_HW_SW_SPLIT.md`) and `docs/design/MARK_II_AREA_PLAN.md` levers L2, L6, L8 and L10 get amended in the first split round from 11-01. The split stays on hold until then.

[A10] **Owner decision (2026-11-13 06:47):** "8x8 is a must, 2if parts an option, but keep it going."
- The flip needs 8x8 as well as 1x1/1if: at least 8x8/1if.
- The two-interface parts are optional. A blocker at 2if only may be deferred to #890 as tracked debt instead of costing a new round.
- #810 continues in its current scope; nothing is re-scoped now.
- Consequence: the flip check must also hold the rows at 8x8/1if. #894 models only 1x1/1if so far, so modelling the 8x8/1if point is its next step after round 4.

[A10] Rulings on the dev sync's round-2 REVIEW READY (issuecomment-6930817036), and a correction of mine.

**Correction: the timing floor.** The resource gate (#818) passes a route set when the best of the recipe's three directives meets **+0.030 ns setup and 0 ns hold** at every signoff corner. My lane prompts since 11-15 wrote "WNS/WHS >= +0.030 ns", which applied the setup floor to hold. That is my error, not the lanes'. Re-graded against #818:
- **Split 1x1/1if at the base:** WNS +0.208, WHS +0.014 on ExtraPostPlacementOpt: **meets**.
- **Split 8x8/1if at the base:** ExtraTimingOpt +0.171 / +0.014 and AltSpreadLogic_high +0.215 / +0.014: **meets**.
- **Every lane's "hold miss" of +0.014 to +0.015 ns is a pass.** Only true setup misses count.
- **#927 is therefore not a flip blocker.** It leaves the flip train and lands after the flip on its own merits. Its cuts add setup margin where 8x8/1if is placement-thin, and they change the release gateware (the meter), which the flip need not carry. If the composed flip head misses #818 at either split shape, #927 comes back in.

**Q1: the 8x8/1if LeaveAll row.** Every late frame waits for lwSRP's join timer, one JoinTime after the participant's previous transmission. IEEE 802.1Q-2018 10.7.4.1 makes that the transmit opportunity: a LeaveAll goes out at the next transmit opportunity after the LeaveAll timer expires. The design already counts "one a JoinTime a participant" (SPLIT_CONTROL_MEMORY.md, THE TRANSMIT). A protocol-mandated wait is not CPU service time.
- THE TRANSMIT's MRPDU row (FR_NFR.md 3.4.1) is measured from the participant's transmit opportunity, not from the LeaveAll timer's expiry, and its bound is unchanged.
- The harness adds a conformance check that a LeaveAll goes out at the first transmit opportunity after expiry, with a planted defect that skips one.
- This is harness grading, so the sync's round 3 owns it. It also clears #901's valid-destinations leg at 1x1/1if, which fails on the same wait. The row's bound does not move.

**Q2: the paced SET_CONFIGURATION record, 305 against 300 at 1x1/1if.** #898 round 7 restates it to 305 with `CTRL_LOOP_TX_MS` 35 at 1x1/1if by the rule (#897 issuecomment-6928240632), and #898 lands before this sync. The sync regrades on #898's merge. It changes neither constant itself.

**Q3: the release AX7101 1x1 route.** Hold +0.014 to +0.016 ns meets #818's 0 ns hold floor, so it passes.

**Sync round 3:** Q1's grading change and its check, then the regrade on the train once #898 merges.

**Owner decision (2026-11-20 17:1x): the flip train's 1x1/1if margins.**

- **The situation:** the SRP cut (#665's ruling of 2026-11-20, item 3) brings 8x8/1if within its 0.75 load ceiling: 0.7436, with no statement exceeded. Its code-layout and cache effects move four 1x1/1if costs past their statements: the paced map edit, the held SET_STREAM_INFO, the ADP record and the centisecond tick. Restated by the usual rule, they put 1x1/1if's last queued notice at 141.53 ms (bound 140) and ACMP at 32.74 ms (bound 30).
- **Decided by the owner:** item 4 of that ruling applies at 1x1/1if here too. The two stale notice-path statements are restated from the fresh every-source measurement of the final image, by the usual rule: the AECP notice item 210 to 150 us, and the long notice 365 to 315 us. The four moved costs are restated by the rule.
  - The 1x1/1if rows are then: last queued notice 132.93 ms (bound 140), ACMP 29.01 ms (bound 30), txL 47.83 ms (bound 49).
  - No owner bound moves.
- **Records:** the exception is named in the train's record and in each restated statement's comment. Round 29's rule otherwise stands.

# [A783] S12b BENCH RE-CHECK on the train's final head `8c5e2b4f`

**Outcome: ONE NEW DUT BLOCKER, at 1x1/1if (h): ACMP GET_TX_STATE_RESPONSE never sets REGISTERING_FAILED** (Milan
v1.2 Table 5.47; Findings). The 1x1/1if run was stopped at the next replay boundary. The fixes under re-check are all
verified, and 8x8/1if has no new DUT failure.

- **8x8/1if:** (a)-(h) done.
  - **Full concurrency:** 8 inputs + 8 outputs + CRF both ways at once, 276 s and then the 1 h soak, with every DUT
    error counter 0.
  - **#946 met:** every input receives, UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT 0.
  - **#943 met:** each output's GET_STREAM_INFO destination is the one its frames go to.
- **1x1/1if:** (a)-(g) done. **F-G5's acceptance met:** a changed input format is kept across a power cycle.
  (h) ran every queued replay but the two that need the tap's capture host (BENCH-BLOCKED anyway); it found the new
  blocker.
- **#951 met as the issue states:** the re-declare hold-off after a MAAP conflict is 30.26-30.27 s. The plan's check
  window ends at 30 s; that is for the owner.

**Images** (the composition lane's builds at `8c5e2b4f`, `--eth-port e2`; every file copied and checked):
- 8x8/1if: bitstream `7d903412`, firmware `d67fd049`;
- 1x1/1if: bitstream `c7189218`, firmware `c873a0aa`.

**Bench:** the DUT's port e2, through the inline 1G tap, to the test machine.
- **The test machine:** a real-time kernel with CPUs 1-3 isolated and AF_XDP zero-copy support, its system clock on
  NTP, gPTP on its PHC only.
- **Its stream tool:** a non-spinning AF_XDP talker and listener with PHC media timing.
- **The harness's emulated entity M** keeps the control protocols (ACMP, MSRP, MAAP); for the concurrency items the
  stream tool sends and receives.
- **The tap's capture host** does not answer, so the two replays that need it are BENCH-BLOCKED.

## 8x8/1if

| Item | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| (a) flash, cold boot | PASS | the bitstream hash written = the published one; one boot and one ready line; BOOTSTS 0x1, no CRC error |
| (b) identity | PASS | ID and VERSION match the manifest; ENTITY 0 "Milan FPGA 8x8", firmware 2.96.0; only the runtime available_index differs from the image's AEM |
| (c) enumeration | PASS | 124 descriptors, 123 identical to the image's own AEM; ENTITY 0's runtime available_index |
| (d) gPTP | PASS | 661 s; the test machine the only grandmaster; asCapable throughout; pdelay 578-584 ns |
| (e) streams | PASS (bench-only counts) | **#946's acceptance met**; **full concurrency PASS**; **#943's acceptance met** (below) |
| (f) 40 cold cycles | **PASS, 40/40 clean** | each boot clean (ready ≤ 1.81 s), the saved binding restored and flowing (≤ 28.5 s), gPTP locked (≤ 13.5 s), every DUT error counter 0; not even a bench-attributed count |
| (g) 1 h soak, 8 in + 8 out + CRF both ways flowing | **PASS** | 3,576 s: each input 28.6 M frames (8,001/s), CRF 1.79 M (500/s), every DUT error counter 0; every output flowing, 0 sequence gaps at the test machine; #943 again met |
| (h) the replica's failed scenarios | no new DUT failure | below |

**(e):**
- **#946:** inputs 1-7, each bound alone, receive 80,002-96,003 frames per 10 s with UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT 0 and every other
  error counter 0. All eight receive at once, each from its own stream, in the concurrency step. An input narrowed to
  4 channels and then bound receives.
- **Full concurrency, 276 s:** inputs 0-7 2,208,066 frames each (8,007/s), the CRF input 137,908 (500/s), outputs 0-7
  8,000-8,001/s and the CRF output 500/s. **Every DUT error counter 0**, AVB_INTERFACE and CLOCK_DOMAIN included; 0
  sequence gaps at the test machine.
  - The test machine's talker: 18.8 M frames, 0 errors, 0 past its presentation offset.
  - Its listener: 0 ring drops. Its CPUs 0-3 at 12/33/61/11 %, no RCU stall.
- **#943:** each output's GET_STREAM_INFO `stream_dest_mac` equals the MAAP destination its frames go to, with
  STREAM_DEST_MAC_VALID set (all 9 outputs, in the concurrency step and again in the soak).
- **Bench-only counts:** one sequence gap per output at the harness's own listener, each within its receive drops.
- **Not counted:** two inputs on one stream (F-G2, #948): the first input receives nothing, as before.

**(h)** (the replica's failed scenarios; the Ethernet stop/start a PHY-level renegotiation, the recorded deviation):
- **PASS now, failed before:** the two REGISTERING checks (REGISTERING is now set), with every earlier pass still passing.
- **The same as the release:** the certification_version check (the owner-signed plan divergence).
- **Harness, as before:** the second-format check (the descriptor lists one format); the persistence scenario's mapping
  step (it maps onto ports without clusters); the two scenarios that unroll their loop for 2 outputs.
- **Harness, newly reachable: the media-clock restart (mr) check.**
  - With #943 fixed it finds the DUT's frames for the first time, and holds in 3 of its 4 windows.
  - In the fourth (the clock-source stream bound again while the DUT is the grandmaster), the emulated entity M did not
    restart its CRF talker in the window. It withdrew it as having "no Listener", although the capture shows the DUT
    declaring Listener Ready 3 ms after the bind, as in the window that passes.
  - With no clock-source stream to re-lock to, there was no restart to signal.
- **For the owner, #951:** after a MAAP conflict the DUT re-declares the moved StreamID **30.262 s and 30.269 s** after
  its Leave (measured on the plan's capture). That is #951's ruling: two longest LeaveAll periods plus JoinTime and one
  transmit, about 30.2 s. The plan's check window ends at 30 s.
- **DUT, known (reported in #943, not changed):** no unsolicited GET_STREAM_INFO on a STREAM_OUTPUT's Listener
  registration change (Milan v1.2 Table 5.22). The solicited answers are right, REGISTERING and REGISTERING_FAILED
  included.
- **Undetermined, minor, as before:** discovery after a link-up. The first ENTITY_AVAILABLE came 5.76 s after the DUT's
  first frame, with a grandmaster change at +4.05 s (3 of 5 runs so far, each with such a change).

## The latency adds at 8x8/1if

**The presentation-offset sweep** (full concurrency, the test machine's talker offset lowered step by step, 96 s per step):

| Talker offset | DUT LATE_TIMESTAMP, 8 AAF inputs + CRF | The talker's max send lateness |
|---|---|---|
| 2 ms | 0 | 76 µs |
| 1 ms | 0 | 97 µs |
| 500 µs | 0 | 79 µs |
| 250 µs | 0 | 82 µs |
| 125 µs | 10 of 6.14 M AAF frames (inputs 4-7: 1, 2, 3, 4) | 75 µs |

- **The hold:** clean from 2 ms down to 250 µs; every other input counter 0 too.
- **The listener floor on this bench:** between 125 and 250 µs.
  - At 125 µs the late frames grow with each stream's place in the talker's per-period send batch, and the talker sends
    each batch up to 75-97 µs late.
  - So the bench's share is most of that budget; it is not separable from the DUT's without the DUT's own ts_delta.
- **Not read: the listener's ts_delta, the per-stage latency taps and the playout FIFO fill.** Neither gating image has
  a path to its CSRs.
  - The console runs `milan_status` and `milan_gettime` only. The images have no bus bridge, and the soft core has no
    JTAG debug.
  - At 8x8/1if the latency taps are pruned (structural zeros).
  - The ts_delta register covers STREAM_INPUT 0 alone, and the taps count at 50 MHz, not 100 MHz.
  - **Needs a decision:** a diagnostic image with a CSR read path, from the composition lane.
- **The DUT talker's capture-to-wire:** not measurable here. Its frames reach the test machine up to 2.03 ms before
  their presentation time, more than the 2 ms transit, so "2 ms minus the earliest arrival" bounds nothing.

## Findings

**New DUT failures: one, a BLOCKER at 1x1/1if.** Every item and replay was triaged as DUT, harness or bench.

- **NEW DUT BLOCKER: ACMP GET_TX_STATE_RESPONSE never sets REGISTERING_FAILED.**
  - **Seen:** at 1x1/1if, after a Listener Asking Failed for STREAM_OUTPUT 0, its flags read 0x0000 (twice, 5 s and
    45 s after). The same moment's GET_STREAM_INFO reports REGISTERING_FAILED 1.
  - **Clause:** Milan v1.2 5.5.4.3 and Table 5.47.
  - **Where, by reading at `8c5e2b4f`:**
    - `third_party/tsn-c-stack/src/acmp.c:1064` sets the flag from the source state's `asking_failed`;
    - the split platform's provider always writes `out->asking_failed = false;`
      (`sw/firmware/ctrl/plat/ctrl_plat.c:96-103`);
    - the SRP and AECP wrappers only forward it (`sw/firmware/ctrl/app/ctrl_app_srp.c:17-21`,
      `sw/firmware/ctrl/app/ctrl_app_aecp.c:17-21`), and nothing else in `sw/firmware` writes it.
  - **Scope:** the same code serves 8x8/1if. The scenario cannot reach this step there (it handles 2 outputs only), and
    the earlier image never reached it (it stopped at REGISTERING, now fixed).
  - **Proposed fix:** fill `asking_failed` from SRP's Listener registration state for the source, the state the
    GET_STREAM_INFO face already reports as REGISTERING_FAILED. Add a host test of GET_TX_STATE after a Listener
    Asking Failed. Not chased.

- **Fixed and verified here:** #946 (every input's format), #943 (the output's destination in GET_STREAM_INFO), F-G5
  (1x1/1if: a format change kept across a power cycle), #951 (the hold-off, as the issue states), REGISTERING on a
  STREAM_OUTPUT.
- **For the owner, #951:** the plan's MAAP-conflict check wants 29-30 s; the DUT re-declares at 30.26-30.27 s, the value
  #951's ruling derives.
- **DUT, known, not changed (reported in #943):** no unsolicited GET_STREAM_INFO on a STREAM_OUTPUT's Listener
  registration change.
- **Undetermined, minor:** discovery after a link-up with a grandmaster change about 4-5 s in.
- **Not counted:** two inputs on one stream (F-G2, #948).
- **Needs a decision:** the ts_delta, latency-tap and playout-fill readings need an image with a CSR read path.
